title: HTTP hook
description: POSTs the event JSON (Content-Type: application/json) to a URL; the 2xx JSON response body uses the same output format as command hooks. Non-2xx, connection failure and non-JSON bodies are non-blocking errors; it cannot block through the status code. Subject to allowedHttpHookUrls and httpHookAllowedEnvVars.

type.description: Handler type: `http` sends an HTTP POST request.
type.title: Type

url.description: URL to send the POST request to.
url.title: Url

headers.description: Additional HTTP headers. Values support `$VAR_NAME` / `${VAR_NAME}` interpolation, but only for variables listed in `allowedEnvVars` (others become empty strings).
headers.title: Headers

allowedEnvVars.description: Environment variable names that may be interpolated into header values. Required for any interpolation to work; further limited by the settings key httpHookAllowedEnvVars.
allowedEnvVars.title: Allowed Env Vars

timeout.description: Seconds before the handler is canceled. Default 600 for command, http and mcp_tool; lowered to 30 on UserPromptSubmit, PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch and to 10 on MessageDisplay. SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5 s budget (raised to the largest per-hook timeout, max 60 s). Not enforced on a command hook running with `async: true`.
timeout.title: Timeout

statusMessage.description: Custom spinner message displayed while the handler runs.
statusMessage.title: Status Message

once.description: If true, the hook is removed after its first successful run (a failed, exit-2 or timed-out run keeps it). Only honored for hooks declared in skill frontmatter; ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter.
once.title: Once

if.description: Permission-rule-syntax filter (exactly one rule, e.g. `Bash(git *)`, `Edit(*.ts)`, `PowerShell(Remove-Item *)`); the handler only runs when the tool call matches. Evaluated only on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied; on any other event a handler with `if` never runs. There is no `&&`/`||`/list syntax: use one handler per condition. Best-effort filter, not a security boundary.
if.title: If

onFailure.title: On Failure
onFailure.description: Whether the action that triggered the hook goes ahead when the hook fails (it could not start, timed out, exited with a code other than 0 or 2, or printed invalid JSON): `continue` lets it through and reports the failure; `block` counts the failure as exit code 2. Ignored for async hooks and on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle.
